sanskrit: tāṃ tu pārśve sthitāṃ prahvāṃ rāmaḥ saṃprekṣya maithilīm hṛdayāntargatakrodho vyāhartum upacakrame
english: Seeing Maithilī standing humbly at his side, Rāma — his anger held within his heart — began to speak.

sanskrit: eṣāsi nirjitā bhadre śatruṃ jitvā mayā raṇe pauruṣād yad anuṣṭheyaṃ tad etad upapāditam
english: "You have been won back, fair one, with my enemy vanquished in battle; what a man of honour was bound to do, that I have accomplished.

sanskrit: gato 'smy antam amarṣasya dharṣaṇā saṃpramārjitā avamānaś ca śatruś ca mayā yugapad uddhṛtau
english: I have put an end to my indignation; the affront has been wiped clean; dishonour and enemy — both have been uprooted by me at the same time.

sanskrit: adya me pauruṣaṃ dṛṣṭam adya me saphalaḥ śramaḥ adya tīrṇapratijñatvāt prabhavāmīha cātmanaḥ
english: Today my manly vigour stands proven; today my toil has borne fruit; today, having fulfilled my vow, I am master of myself.

sanskrit: yā tvaṃ virahitā nītā calacittena rakṣasā daivasaṃpādito doṣo mānuṣeṇa mayā jitaḥ
english: You were carried off by a fickle-minded Rākṣasa — that fault wrought by fate has been overcome by me, a mortal.

sanskrit: saṃprāptam avamānaṃ yas tejasā na pramārjati kas tasya puruṣārtho 'sti puruṣasyālpatejasaḥ
english: What purpose of man does that man of feeble spirit serve, who does not wipe away with his valour the dishonour he has received?

sanskrit: laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya laṅkāyāś cāvamardanam saphalaṃ tasya tac chlāghyam adya karma hanūmataḥ
english: Today that praiseworthy act of Hanūmat — the crossing of the ocean and the trampling of Laṅkā — has borne its fruit.

sanskrit: yuddhe vikramataś caiva hitaṃ mantrayataś ca me sugrīvasya sasainyasya saphalo 'dya pariśramaḥ
english: Today the exertion of Sugrīva, who strove valiantly in battle and counselled my welfare together with his army, has borne its fruit.

sanskrit: nirguṇaṃ bhrātaraṃ tyaktvā yo māṃ svayam upasthitaḥ vibhīṣaṇasya bhaktasya saphalo 'dya pariśramaḥ
english: Today the effort of the devoted Vibhīṣaṇa — who, abandoning his worthless brother, came to me of his own accord — has borne its fruit.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bruvatas tasya sītā rāmasya tad vacaḥ mṛgīvotphullanayanā babhūvāśrupariplutā
english: As Rāma spoke these words, Sītā — her eyes wide open like a doe's — was flooded with tears.

sanskrit: paśyatas tāṃ tu rāmasya bhūyaḥ krodho 'bhyavartata prabhūtājyāvasiktasya pāvakasyeva dīpyataḥ
english: As Rāma looked upon her, his anger flared up afresh, blazing like a fire fed with copious ghee.

sanskrit: sa baddhvā bhrukuṭiṃ vaktre tiryakprekṣitalocanaḥ abravīt paruṣaṃ sītāṃ madhye vānararakṣasām
english: With furrowed brow and eyes cast askance, he spoke harshly to Sītā in the midst of the monkeys and Rākṣasas:

sanskrit: yat kartavyaṃ manuṣyeṇa dharṣaṇāṃ parimārjatā tat kṛtaṃ sakalaṃ sīte śatruhastād amarṣaṇāt
english: "Whatever a man must do to wipe away an outrage, all of that has been done, O Sītā, in my fury against the enemy.

sanskrit: nirjitā jīvalokasya tapasā bhāvitātmanā agastyena durādharṣā muninā dakṣiṇeva dik
english: As the southern quarter was subdued by the sage Agastya — his soul perfected by asceticism — hard to overcome in all the world, so has the foe been vanquished.

sanskrit: viditaś cāstu bhadraṃ te yo 'yaṃ raṇapariśramaḥ sa tīrṇaḥ suhṛdāṃ vīryān na tvadarthaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ
english: Know well, fair one, that this toil of battle was undertaken and brought to completion through the valour of friends — not for your sake by me.

sanskrit: rakṣatā tu mayā vṛttam apavādaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ prakhyātasyātmavaṃśasya nyaṅgaṃ ca parimārjatā
english: It was undertaken by me to safeguard my conduct, to ward off reproach on every side, and to wipe clean the stain on my celebrated lineage.

sanskrit: prāptacāritrasaṃdehā mama pratimukhe sthitā dīpo netrāturasyeva pratikūlāsi me dṛḍham
english: Now that suspicion has arisen about your chastity, your standing before me is as offensive to me as a lamp is to one whose eyes are afflicted.

sanskrit: tad gaccha hy abhyanujñātā yateṣṭaṃ janakātmaje etā daśa diśo bhadre kāryam asti na me tvayā
english: Therefore, O daughter of Janaka, you are dismissed — go wherever you wish, to these ten directions; I have no further need of you.

sanskrit: kaḥ pumān hi kule jātaḥ striyaṃ paragṛhoṣitām tejasvi punar ādadyāt suhṛllekhena cetasā
english: For what man of noble birth and self-respect, his heart guided by good counsel, would take back a woman who has lived in another's house?

sanskrit: rāvaṇāṅkaparibhraṣṭāṃ dṛṣṭāṃ duṣṭena cakṣuṣā kathaṃ tvāṃ punarādadyāṃ kulaṃ vyapadiśan mahat
english: How could I take you back again — you who have fallen from Rāvaṇa's lap and been beheld by his lustful eyes — I, who declare my lineage to be great?

sanskrit: tadarthaṃ nirjitā me tvaṃ yaśaḥ pratyāhṛtaṃ mayā nāsti me tvayy abhiṣvaṅgo yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatām itaḥ
english: The war was fought for that purpose; my honour has been retrieved by me; I have no attachment to you — depart hence wherever you please.

sanskrit: iti pravyāhṛtaṃ bhadre mayaitat kṛtabuddhinā lakṣmaṇe bharate vā tvaṃ kuru buddhiṃ yathāsukham
english: This, fair one, I have declared with a settled mind. Set your heart, if you wish, on Lakṣmaṇa or on Bharata.

sanskrit: sugrīve vānarendre vā rākṣasendre vibhīṣaṇe niveśaya manaḥ sīte yathā vā sukham ātmanaḥ
english: Or fix your mind upon Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, or upon Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, O Sītā — or wherever your own happiness lies.

sanskrit: na hi tvāṃ rāvaṇo dṛṣṭvā divyarūpāṃ manoramām marṣayate ciraṃ sīte svagṛhe parivartinīm
english: For Rāvaṇa, beholding you of divine form and captivating beauty dwelling in his own abode, would not have endured it long without consummating his desire.

sanskrit: tataḥ priyārhaśvaraṇā tad apriyaṃ priyād upaśrutya cirasya maithilī mumoca bāṣpaṃ subhṛśaṃ pravepitā gajendrahastābhihateva vallarī
english: Then Maithilī, worthy to receive love at his feet, hearing those unwelcome words from her beloved after so long, burst into profuse weeping, trembling like a vine struck by the trunk of a lordly elephant.

sanskrit: evam uktā tu vaidehī paruṣaṃ lomaharṣaṇam rāghaveṇa saroṣeṇa bhṛśaṃ pravyathitābhavat
english: Thus addressed with harsh and hair-raising words by the wrathful Rāghava, Vaidehī was deeply distressed.

sanskrit: sā tad aśrutapūrvaṃ hi jane mahati maithilī śrutvā bhartṛvaco rūkṣaṃ lajjayā vrīḍitābhavat
english: Hearing those rough words of her husband — words never heard before — in that great assembly, Maithilī was overwhelmed with shame.

sanskrit: praviśantīva gātrāṇi svāny eva janakātmajā vākśalyais taiḥ saśalyeva bhṛśam aśrūṇy avartayat
english: The daughter of Janaka, as though pierced to the quick by those verbal shafts, seemed to sink into herself, and shed copious tears.

sanskrit: tato bāṣpaparikliṣṭaṃ pramārjantī svam ānanam śanair gadgadayā vācā bhartāram idam abravīt
english: Then, wiping her face wet with tears, she spoke these words to her husband in a slow, choked voice:

sanskrit: kiṃ mām asadṛśaṃ vākyam īdṛśaṃ śrotradāruṇam rūkṣaṃ śrāvayase vīra prākṛtaḥ prākṛtām iva
english: "Why do you cause me to hear such unworthy and ear-searing harsh words, O hero — as a vulgar man speaks to a common woman?

sanskrit: na tathāsmi mahābāho yathā tvam avagacchasi pratyayaṃ gaccha me svena cāritreṇaiva te śape
english: I am not as you imagine, O great-armed one. Know me truly — I swear to you by my own conduct.

sanskrit: pṛthak strīṇāṃ pracāreṇa jātiṃ tvaṃ pariśaṅkase parityajemāṃ śaṅkāṃ tu yadi te 'haṃ parīkṣitā
english: You suspect the whole class on account of the ways of lowly women; abandon this suspicion — I am one who has been tested.

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ gātrasaṃsparśaṃ gatāsmi vivaśā prabho kāmakāro na me tatra daivaṃ tatrāparādhyati
english: If, O lord, I came into bodily contact against my will, the fault is not mine there — it is fate that is to blame.

sanskrit: madadhīnaṃ tu yat tan me hṛdayaṃ tvayi vartate parādhīneṣu gātreṣu kiṃ kariṣyāmy anīśvarā
english: But what is under my control — my heart — that abides in you; what could I do, powerless, over a body under another's control?

sanskrit: sahasaṃvṛddhabhāvāc ca saṃsargeṇa ca mānada yady ahaṃ te na vijñātā hatā tenāsmi śāśvatam
english: If I am not known to you through our shared upbringing and intimacy, O giver of honour, then I am forever destroyed by that.

sanskrit: preṣitas te yadā vīro hanūmān avalokakaḥ laṅkāsthāhaṃ tvayā vīra kiṃ tadā na visarjitā
english: When your hero Hanūmat was sent to find me and I was in Laṅkā, why were you not pleased to have me abandoned then, O hero?

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ vānarendrasya tvadvākyasamanantaram tvayā saṃtyaktayā vīra tyaktaṃ syāj jīvitaṃ mayā
english: In the presence of the lord of monkeys, immediately upon receiving your message, I — being abandoned by you, O hero — would have given up my life.

sanskrit: na vṛthā te śramo 'yaṃ syāt saṃśaye nyasya jīvitam suhṛjjanaparikleśo na cāyaṃ niṣphalas tava
english: Your toil would not have been in vain, having laid down my life in doubt, and the suffering of your allies would not have been fruitless.

sanskrit: tvayā tu naraśārdūla krodham evānuvartatā laghuneva manuṣyeṇa strītvam eva puraskṛtam
english: But you, O tiger among men, following only your anger, have given precedence — as a shallow man would — merely to the fact of my womanhood.

sanskrit: apadeśena janakān notpattir vasudhātalāt mama vṛttaṃ ca vṛttajña bahu te na puraskṛtam
english: My origin not from Janaka but from the earth's surface, and my conduct — you who are learned in conduct — has not been given weight by you.

sanskrit: na pramāṇīkṛtaḥ pāṇir bālye bālena pīḍitaḥ mama bhaktiś ca śīlaṃ ca sarvaṃ te pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtam
english: The hand clasped in childhood, pressed by a child, my devotion and my character — all of this you have cast behind you.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇā rudatī bāṣpagadgadabhāṣiṣī abravīl lakṣmaṇaṃ sītā dīnaṃ dhyānaparaṃ sthitam
english: Speaking thus, weeping, her voice faltering with sobs, Sītā addressed Lakṣmaṇa, who stood absorbed in thought, downcast:

sanskrit: citāṃ me kuru saumitre vyasanasyāsya bheṣajam mithyāpavādopahatā nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: "Build me a pyre, O son of Sumitrā — that is the remedy for this calamity. Struck down by a false accusation, I have no wish to live.

sanskrit: aprītasya guṇair bhartus tyaktayā janasaṃsadi yā kṣamā me gatir gantuṃ pravekṣye havyavāhanam
english: Forsaken in a public assembly by a husband who takes no pleasure in my virtues, the only course befitting me is to enter the fire."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vaidehyā lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā amarṣavaśam āpanno rāghavānanam aikṣata
english: Addressed thus by Vaidehī, Lakṣmaṇa — the slayer of enemy heroes — fell under the sway of indignation and looked towards Rāghava's face.

sanskrit: sa vijñāya manaśchandaṃ rāmasyākārasūcitam citāṃ cakāra saumitrir mate rāmasya vīryavān
english: Understanding Rāma's wish as indicated by his demeanour, the valiant son of Sumitrā built the pyre in accordance with Rāma's intent.

sanskrit: adhomukhaṃ tato rāmaṃ śanaiḥ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam upāsarpata vaidehī dīpyamānaṃ hutāśanam
english: Then Vaidehī, after slowly circumambulating Rāma with his face cast downward, approached the blazing fire.

sanskrit: praṇamya devatābhyaś ca brāhmaṇebhyaś ca maithilī baddhāñjalipuṭā cedam uvācāgnisamīpataḥ
english: Maithilī, bowing to the gods and the Brāhmaṇas, stood near the fire with hands folded in reverence and spoke thus:

sanskrit: yathā me hṛdayaṃ nityaṃ nāpasarpati rāghavāt tathā lokasya sākṣī māṃ sarvataḥ pātu pāvakaḥ
english: "As my heart has never strayed from Rāghava, so may Pāvaka, the witness of all worlds, protect me on every side."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu vaidehī parikramya hutāśanam viveśa jvalanaṃ dīptaṃ niḥsaṅgenāntarātmanā
english: Having spoken thus and circumambulated the fire, Vaidehī entered the blazing flames with a heart utterly serene and free of attachment.

sanskrit: janaḥ sa sumahāṃs tatra bālavṛddhasamākulaḥ dadarśa maithilīṃ tatra praviśantīṃ hutāśanam
english: That vast assembly gathered there — thronged with young and old alike — witnessed Maithilī entering the fire.

sanskrit: tasyām agniṃ viśantyāṃ tu hāheti vipulaḥ svanaḥ rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca saṃbabhūvādbhutopamaḥ
english: As she entered the fire, a great cry of "Alas! Alas!" arose among the Rākṣasas and the monkeys — a sound beyond all wonder.

sanskrit: tato vaiśravaṇo rājā yamaś cāmitrakarśanaḥ sahasrākṣo mahendraś ca varuṇaś ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then Vaiśravaṇa the king, and Yama the afflicitor of foes, and the thousand-eyed Mahendra, and the scorching Varuṇa —

sanskrit: ṣaḍardhanayanaḥ śrīmān mahādevo vṛṣadhvajaḥ kartā sarvasya lokasya brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ
english: — and the glorious three-eyed Mahādeva whose banner bears the bull, and Brahmā the creator of all worlds, best among knowers of Brahman —

sanskrit: ete sarve samāgamya vimānaiḥ sūryasaṃnibhaiḥ āgamya nagarīṃ laṅkām abhijagmuś ca rāghavam
english: — all of these assembled together and, arriving at the city of Laṅkā in celestial chariots bright as the sun, approached Rāghava.

sanskrit: tataḥ sahastābharaṇān pragṛhya vipulān bhujān abruvaṃs tridaśaśreṣṭhāḥ prāñjaliṃ rāghavaṃ sthitam
english: Then the chiefs of the thirty gods, raising their broad arms adorned with bracelets, addressed Rāghava as he stood with hands reverently joined:

sanskrit: kartā sarvasya lokasya śreṣṭho jñānavatāṃ varaḥ upekṣase kathaṃ sītāṃ patantīṃ havyavāhane kathaṃ devagaṇaśreṣṭham ātmānaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: "You are the creator of all worlds, the foremost among the wise, best of all. How can you disregard Sītā as she falls into the fire? How do you not know yourself to be the chief among the hosts of gods?"

sanskrit: ṛtadhāmā vasuḥ pūrvaṃ vasūnāṃ ca prajāpatiḥ tvaṃ trayāṇāṃ hi lokānām ādikartā svayaṃprabhuḥ
english: "You were formerly Ṛtadhāman, a Vasu, lord of the Vasus — you are the primordial creator of the three worlds, self-luminous.

sanskrit: rudrāṇām aṣṭamo rudraḥ sādhyānām api pañcamaḥ aśvinau cāpi te karṇau candrasūryau ca cakṣuṣī
english: You are the eighth Rudra among the Rudras, and the fifth among the Sādhyas; the two Aśvins are your ears, and the moon and sun your two eyes.

sanskrit: ante cādau ca lokānāṃ dṛśyase tvaṃ paraṃtapa upekṣase ca vaidehīṃ mānuṣaḥ prākṛto yathā
english: You are seen at the beginning and end of the worlds, O scorcher of foes — yet you ignore Vaidehī as though you were an ordinary mortal.

sanskrit: ity ukto lokapālais taiḥ svāmī lokasya rāghavaḥ abravīt tridaśaśreṣṭhān rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Thus addressed by those guardians of the worlds, Rāghava — lord of the worlds, Rāma, best of those who uphold dharma — spoke to the chiefs of the thirty gods:

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ mānuṣaṃ manye rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam yo 'haṃ yasya yataś cāhaṃ bhagavāṃs tad bravītu me
english: "I consider myself a mortal man, Rāma the son of Daśaratha. Who I am, whose I am, and whence I am — let the blessed one tell me that."

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇaṃ kākutsthaṃ brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ abravīc chṛṇu me rāma satyaṃ satyaparākrama
english: To Kākutstha speaking thus, Brahmā — best among knowers of Brahman — said: "Hear the truth from me, O Rāma of true valour:

sanskrit: bhavān nārāyaṇo devaḥ śrīmāṃś cakrāyudho vibhuḥ ekaśṛṅgo varāhas tvaṃ bhūtabhavyasapatnajit
english: You are the god Nārāyaṇa, the glorious, the all-pervading lord who wields the discus; you are the boar with a single tusk, the vanquisher of foes past and future.

sanskrit: akṣaraṃ brahmasatyaṃ ca madhye cānte ca rāghava lokānāṃ tvaṃ paro dharmo viṣvaksenaś caturbhujaḥ
english: You are the imperishable, the truth of Brahman, in the middle and at the end, O Rāghava; you are the supreme dharma of the worlds, Viṣvaksena, four-armed.

sanskrit: śārṅgadhanvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ puruṣaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ajitaḥ khaḍgadhṛg viṣṇuḥ kṛṣṇaś caiva bṛhadbalaḥ
english: You are Śārṅgadhanvan, Hṛṣīkeśa, the Puruṣa, Puruṣottama, the Unconquered, the sword-bearer, Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, and the immensely powerful one.

sanskrit: senānīr grāmaṇīś ca tvaṃ buddhiḥ sattvaṃ kṣamā damaḥ prabhavaś cāpyayaś ca tvam upendro madhusūdanaḥ
english: You are the general of armies and the village chief; you are intellect, being, patience, and restraint; you are the source and dissolution; you are Upendra and Madhusūdana.

sanskrit: indrakarmā mahendras tvaṃ padmanābho raṇāntakṛt śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ ca tvām āhur divyā maharṣayaḥ
english: You are the one who acts like Indra, great Mahendra, Padmanābha, the destroyer of enemies in battle; the divine great sages call you the refuge and the shelter.

sanskrit: sahasraśṛṅgo vedātmā śatajihvo maharṣabhaḥ tvaṃ yajñas tvaṃ vaṣaṭkāras tvam oṃkāraḥ paraṃtapa
english: You are the thousand-horned, the soul of the Vedas, the hundred-tongued, the great bull; you are the sacrifice, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are the syllable Oṃ, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: prabhavaṃ nidhanaṃ vā te na viduḥ ko bhavān iti dṛśyase sarvabhūteṣu brāhmaṇeṣu ca goṣu ca
english: None knows your origin or your end, nor who you are; you are seen in all beings, in Brāhmaṇas, and in cows.

sanskrit: dikṣu sarvāsu gagane parvateṣu vaneṣu ca sahasracaraṇaḥ śrīmāñ śataśīrṣaḥ sahasradhṛk
english: In all directions, in the sky, in mountains and in forests — you of a thousand feet, the glorious, the hundred-headed, the bearer of a thousand weapons.

sanskrit: tvaṃ dhārayasi bhūtāni vasudhāṃ ca saparvatām ante pṛthivyāḥ salile dṛśyase tvaṃ mahoragaḥ
english: You sustain all beings and the earth with its mountains; at the end of the earth you appear in the waters as the great serpent.

sanskrit: trīṃl lokān dhārayan rāma devagandharvadānavān ahaṃ te hṛdayaṃ rāma jihvā devī sarasvatī
english: You uphold the three worlds, O Rāma — gods, Gandharvas, and Dānavas; I, Brahmā, am your heart, O Rāma, and the goddess Sarasvatī your tongue.

sanskrit: devā gātreṣu lomāni nirmitā brahmaṇā prabho nimeṣas te 'bhavad rātrir unmeṣas te 'bhavad divā
english: The gods were fashioned as the hairs of your body by Brahmā, O lord; your closing of the eyes became night, your opening of the eyes became day.

sanskrit: saṃskārās te 'bhavan vedā na tad asti tvayā vinā jagat sarvaṃ śarīraṃ te sthairyaṃ te vasudhātalam
english: The Vedas became your sacraments; nothing exists apart from you; the entire universe is your body, and the steadiness of the earth is your steadfastness.

sanskrit: agniḥ kopaḥ prasādas te somaḥ śrīvatsalakṣaṇa tvayā lokās trayaḥ krāntāḥ purāṇe vikramais tribhiḥ
english: Fire is your wrath and Soma your serenity, O bearer of the Śrīvatsa mark; in ancient times the three worlds were traversed by you with three strides.

sanskrit: mahendraś ca kṛto rājā baliṃ baddhvā mahāsuram sītā lakṣmīr bhavān viṣṇur devaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: Mahendra was made king by you after binding Bali the great Asura; Sītā is Lakṣmī, you are Viṣṇu the god, Kṛṣṇa, Prajāpati.

sanskrit: vadhārthaṃ rāvaṇasyeha praviṣṭo mānuṣīṃ tanum tad idaṃ naḥ kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ tvayā dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: You entered a human body here for the purpose of slaying Rāvaṇa; that purpose of ours has been accomplished by you, O best of those who uphold dharma.

sanskrit: nihato rāvaṇo rāma prahṛṣṭo divam ākrama amoghaṃ balavīryaṃ te amoghas te parākramaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa is slain, O Rāma — ascend to heaven rejoicing; your strength and valour are unfailing, and your heroism is unfailing.

sanskrit: amoghās te bhaviṣyanti bhaktimantaś ca ye narāḥ ye tvāṃ devaṃ dhruvaṃ bhaktāḥ purāṇaṃ puruṣottamam
english: Those mortals who are devoted to you, who are steadfastly devoted to you — the ancient, eternal god, Puruṣottama — will never be frustrated.

sanskrit: ye narāḥ kīrtayiṣyanti nāsti teṣāṃ parābhavaḥ
english: Those mortals who shall glorify you — for them there is no defeat."
